Jack Rudoni converts to give to Coventry their first goal at home since returning to the Premier League! 🙌 https://t.co/Q7la7nYwoq

Mistake by Hornicek and then he appears to bring down Cherif diving to retrieve it.

Yes, definitely a pen even though VAR took its time.

Good atmosphere. The home fans are making a racket.

Noticeable that Yirenkyi slots in being Van Ewijk when the full-back goes forward. Miley, who is playing at right-back, intercepts a chip up to Mason-Clark and works the ball back to Hornicek.

As the strains of We’ll Live and Die in These Towns dies down to segue into the Eton Boating Song, Newcastle kick off, attacking from right to left. When they lose the ball Wissa is penalised for tripping Rudoni 45 yards out.

Coventry are in blue and white stripes, harking back to the 1987 Cup final rather than the Mick Coop years. Newcastle are in vibrant lilac.

It was good to get a win. We worked very hard for it. It’s so hard to get wins, especially on the road. And now we’re back at home and we have to work on those attributes [that earned us the win] at Forest. We rotated pretty well, there are different aspects of the game we want to improve on regardless of shape.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1301. Video: McKennie joins Juventus group training before AZ Alkmaar clash

Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie trained with his teammates at Continassa this morning, on the eve of a Europa League game against AZ Alkmaar.

Juventus are preparing for Thursday’s away Europa League game against Dutch side AZ.

The Bianconeri’s midfielder McKennie was spotted on the pitch alongside his teammates this morning. He warmed up separately with Juan Cabal, then joined the rest of the team for a training game.

Zeki Celik continued training separately today, while Jeff Ekhator will be called up for his first European match.

#1300. Accounting of Africa’s water reveals a management gap

Xu Wang is in the State Key Laboratory of Urban-rural Water Resources and Environment, School of Ecology and Environment, Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, Shenzhen 518055, China.

The water cycle is global, yet its accounting is not. Rain, rivers and underground water cross borders freely, but water use is reported by country. The budget for the world’s total usage is therefore only as reliable as the weakest report. When a country cannot measure usage, its water is lost from global accounting — and with it, any claim to a fair share.

#1299. Pio Esposito: Inter reaction ‘wasn’t a given’, goals are ‘like oxygen’

Francesco Pio Esposito is delighted with Inter’s 3-0 win over Feyenoord, in which he scored for the first time since September 14: ‘Goals are like oxygen.’

The Italian striker scored the second goal of the night for the Nerazzurri, who beat Feyenoord on the road 3-0 on Tuesday.

Cristian Chivu’s men quickly bounced back after a 3-1 derby defeat against Milan in Serie A just a few days earlier.

“It wasn’t a given. We were good at having that reaction against a tough opponent,” Pio told Sky Sport.

“We were good at stepping onto the pitch with the right approach and taking the game where we wanted.

“Surely, we analyse defeats. We did, and I’m happy we put words into action.”

Inter have six points in four Champions League games; do they feel they can still finish in the top eight?

“It’s still very long. We must focus on one game at a time, thinking that we can play on par with everyone until the end,” Pio Esposito said.

His goal against Feyenoord was his first at club level since September 14.

“Surely, a goal is like oxygen for a striker, but I try to put the work for the team ahead of everything else and I’m happy to have ended my drought,” he concluded.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1298. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Tonight’s hosts are yet to qualify for a major tournament and are expected to set up in a defensive shape. England defender Esme Morgan believes the squad are ready for a long night of breaking down a stubborn opposition.

She told a pre-match press conference: “It’s just about persistence and trying not to get drawn into being frustrated by the opposition. A really good example was the away game against Ukraine in qualifying. We couldn’t seem to break through in the first half - the keeper was making saves, we hit the woodwork - but the messaging at half-time was just to keep continuing because we were creating opportunities.

”Not to start snatching or taking shots from distance, just trusting in our style of play and our ability to find gaps. We came out for the second half and scored really quickly. It’s just about sticking to the plan and being patient.”

Erica Meg Parkinson, one of England’s new midfielders, was apparently named after Eric Cantona.

While Cantona still famously is proud of his kung fu kick, when he attacked an obnoxious Crystal Palace fan, Parkison is less enthused by football’s most famous case of breaking the fourth wall.

“My dad is a huge Man United fan so I was named after Eric Cantona,” Parkinson says. “It’s a pretty good player to be named after except for, you know, the karate kicks.

“My brother was named after Denis Law. I don’t think my mum had much of a say in the name so she was dragged into it, but it kind of worked out because we both play football now.”

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1296. Valverde played over 40 minutes injured as Real Madrid face three away games in a week

Real Madrid came away from Camp Nou on Sunday night with three points and a new fitness worry. José Mourinho revealed after the 2-1 win over Barcelona that Fede Valverde had spent a large part of the game carrying an injury, and the timing is far from ideal with three away fixtures to come in the space of seven days.

The coach went out of his way to single out the Uruguayan in his post-match press conference, saying Valverde “played injured for more than 40 minutes”. Mourinho added: “He got injured, wanted to continue, pushed himself to his limits, and gave everything while he was on the field.”

Mourinho did not say what kind of injury Valverde had suffered or at what point in the match it happened. At the time of writing, Real Madrid had not published a medical report on the midfielder, who was named in the starting XI alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni, Bernardo Silva and Jude Bellingham.

The club’s English account still made him one of the faces of the night, sharing a Valverde post shortly after midnight.

🗣️ @FedeeValverde 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/iOcHUMmM90

Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadriden) October 26, 2026

Valverde was not the only fitness story of the weekend. Thibaut Courtois dropped out on matchday because of what the club called a flu-like illness, with Illia Voloshyn called up as cover. Andriy Lunin started in goal and, according to Real Madrid’s own match report, made a fine stop from a Gerard Martín header in the 66th minute.

Mourinho said his only message to Lunin before kick-off was simple: “You train to play, not to sit on the bench. Go and play.” He also stressed that the squad had not been rattled by the late change, adding that “today none of us cried before the match because Thibaut wasn’t playing”. Courtois, whose future has been discussed in terms of a possible one-year contract extension, now has a few days to recover before the next game.

The calendar offers Madrid little breathing space. Mourinho pointed out that “on Sunday we play away; then we play away on Wednesday, and then we have another away match on Saturday”. According to the fixture list, those games are against Racing Santander on 1 November, AEK Athens in the Champions League on 4 November and Valencia on 7 November.

That run is where Mourinho’s faith in his squad will be tested. He insisted after the Clásico that “I have a rich bench, with players who can be starters”, and he backed it up at Camp Nou by leaving Eduardo Camavinga among the substitutes days after his strong display in the 4-1 win over RB Leipzig. Camavinga came on and set up the late winner for Kylian Mbappé.

The victory was Madrid’s fifth in a row and, as Mourinho noted, leaves them three points behind Barcelona rather than six or nine. Keeping that momentum through three away games will be far easier with Valverde available, so the club’s next medical update on the midfielder will be closely watched before the trip to Santander.

#1295. Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three big guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

That was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

“It was a joy to watch,” Arteta said. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

“LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1294. Chinese brands drop Mbappé as backlash hits LaLiga coverage in China

Kylian Mbappé is facing the biggest commercial crisis of his career in China. Three Chinese companies announced on Tuesday that they are ending their agreements with the Real Madrid forward, and the fallout has already reached LaLiga’s television coverage in one of football’s most valuable markets.

The trigger was a short clip linked to the French online show The Bridge. In it, Mbappé is asked which meme of himself he likes most, and he refers to a video of “a guy … I think he was a Chinese dictator”, before an edited picture of his face on the body of Mao Zedong appears, as reported by the Associated Press. The footage has not been independently verified and, according to the BBC, the show has since taken the original upload off its YouTube channel.

Beverage firm Dongpeng, the dairy group Mengniu and Milkground, which makes cheese, all issued statements on Tuesday in very similar language. None of them spelled out exactly what Mbappé had said, but each referred to hurt national feelings. Dongpeng’s statement, carried by the state-run Global Times, ended with the line: “Effective immediately, we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappé.”

Mengniu said it “firmly opposes and has zero tolerance for any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”. Social platform RedNote, whose own content partnership with the player ran out at the end of 2024, said it would take down related promotional material. The Global Times added that Dior, On and Hublot had removed Mbappé content from their Weibo pages, and that new users are currently unable to follow his accounts on RedNote or Weibo.

The row has even reached China’s foreign ministry. Asked about the controversy, a spokesperson said that “words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society”, according to AP.

The part of the story with the widest reach for Spanish football concerns broadcasting. According to the Global Times, Shanghai outlet The Paper reported that China Media Group, the parent organisation of state broadcaster CCTV, has suspended broadcasts of matches involving LaLiga and Mbappé. CCTV’s news apps have also removed content about the striker. Neither LaLiga nor Real Madrid had commented publicly at the time of writing, and there was no indication of how long any suspension might last.

Mbappé himself has not responded either, and The Bridge has stayed silent. The timing is awkward for player and club alike. Only on Sunday he was on the scoresheet as Madrid won the Clásico 2-1 at Camp Nou, a result that came with its own fitness worries over Fede Valverde.

The “dictator” tag has followed Mbappé for some time, partly because of the influence he is said to hold at club and international level, and he has spoken about it before. In a France Football interview in September he said the memes “sometimes reveals a lack of political and human awareness among people”, as quoted by the BBC.

On the pitch, the forward has been in fine form, with goals and assists in recent weeks including the 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig. Off it, the pressure is now on him to address a backlash that is still growing, with Madrid due at Racing Santander on Sunday.

#1292. Espanyol sack Manolo González hours after 121st-minute Copa exit at Sestao River

Jon Rojo's goal in the last minute of extra time gave Sestao River a 4-3 win and knocked Espanyol out of the Copa del Rey. Within hours the club ended Manolo González's time as head coach, five months after confirming he would stay with Monchi's full backing.

Espanyol dismissed head coach Manolo González on Tuesday 27 October 2026, hours after a 4-3 defeat at Sestao River in the Copa del Rey. Defender Jon Rojo won the round of 128 tie at Estadio Las Llanas from a G. Zorrilla assist. He forced home a loose ball in the box in the 121st minute, just as the tie looked to be heading for penalties, EFE reported.

The match was played in heavy rain that left the Las Llanas pitch almost unplayable. Marcos Fernández put Espanyol ahead from the penalty spot after six minutes. Adri Carrión equalised in the 18th minute and Andoni Ugarte made it 2-1 in the 40th, both goals set up by Eneko Delgado Ginés.

Espanyol levelled with a second penalty in the 90th minute. Gabriel Moscardo then put them 3-2 up in the 96th minute. Ander Laka equalised two minutes later before Rojo’s late winner.

The visitors had 61% of the ball against 39% for Sestao River. Espanyol completed 321 accurate passes to Sestao’s 140. Sestao still managed 9 shots on goal to Espanyol’s 6, and Espanyol goalkeeper Marko Dmitrović made 5 saves to the hosts’ 2. Ugarte was the top-rated player on the night with 8.5.

Before the tie, the team had taken only one point from their previous 15 available in LaLiga, according to AFP. Their last six results in all competitions now read five defeats and one draw, with losses to Racing Santander, Atlético Madrid, Elche and Rayo Vallecano and a 1-1 draw with Málaga.

Sestao River, coached by Ángel Viadero, have gone the other way. The win over Espanyol extended a run of five wins and a draw in their last six matches.

The club’s announcement brought González’s tenure to a close after more than three seasons in charge. He had reached his 100th official match against Sevilla on 7 September. That made him the ninth-longest-serving coach by matches in Espanyol’s history.

Espanyol finished 11th in LaLiga in 2025/26 under González, with 12 wins, 10 draws and 16 defeats. Monchi, the new sporting director, had given him full backing at that stage.

✍️ OFICIAL | Manolo González deixa de ser entrenador de l'#RCDE. El Club vol agrair-li la seva feina durant tots aquests anys i li desitja molta sort en els seus projectes futurs.

— RCD Espanyol de Barcelona (@RCDEspanyol) October 27, 2026

On the eve of the tie, González admitted results had been poor. He said he would keep fighting for the club until his final day in the job.

Espanyol must now prepare for a LaLiga trip to Villarreal on Friday 30 October. Sestao River travel to Coruxo in Segunda División RFEF Group 1 on Sunday 1 November. The Copa del Rey second round is scheduled for 2 December under the RFEF’s 2026/27 calendar.

#1291. Urda crash: Copa del Rey ties rescheduled to 13 November, three in international break

The RFEF has spread the 24 Copa del Rey first-round ties postponed after the Urda rail crash across 29 October to 13 November. Valencia, Betis and Celta will now play their ties during the November international break.

A national tragedy has stopped Spanish football. The Royal Spanish Football Federation called off every Copa del Rey first-round tie scheduled for the evening of 28 October. All other matches in competitions it organises were postponed too. The decision was taken out of respect for the victims of the rail crash in Toledo province.

A Renfe high-speed train and an Iryo high-speed train collided near Urda station. The crash killed 68 people and injured 80, Público reported. An investigating judge at the court in Orgaz has ordered the first inquiries into what caused the collision.

The shutdown reached beyond the cup. The federation also postponed the nine first-round matches of the futsal Copa de España. The futsal draw planned for 16:00 on 29 October was cancelled.

Valencia, Betis, Alavés, Celta and Levante were the top-flight clubs due in cup action that evening. Each of them must now squeeze a rearranged tie into its schedule. That extra game has to fit into an already crowded run of league and European fixtures. The timing differs sharply from club to club.

Alavés go first. Regional side Anaitasuna host them at 19:00 on Tuesday 3 November. Levante travel to CD Tarancón two days later, on Thursday 5 November.

Three clubs face a longer wait. Celta close the round away to Salamanca, with kick-off at 21:00 on Friday 13 November. Valencia and Betis are in action earlier that same week. A tie that was meant to be settled in October will now be played while national teams are away.

Mallorca’s tie at CD Alcoyano kicks off at 21:00 on the same Thursday evening, after Levante’s game at Tarancón. COPE’s list of the rearranged ties records Mallorca as a Segunda División side, not a top-flight one.

That league context matters. Three days after the cup tie, Mallorca play a second-tier match away to Andorra. They are still aiming for automatic promotion. A rearranged cup trip now sits directly before a league fixture in that push.

The national first round had been pencilled in for a single evening, 28 October, when the season’s fixtures were drawn up. The 2026/27 calendar originally set the Copa del Rey second round for 2 December.

#1290. Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

I fully know we all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through. We have a big game on Sunday.

This feels a big moment for Carrick and United’s players to answer some of their critics. They have been getting battered from all sides in the last couple of days. Nicky Butt suggested on his podcast that Carrick told him before he got the United job that management “not for me” and “my head’s all over the shop” and that United was the only job he would take. At the very least, those comments are unhelpful and they are thought to have been dimly received internally.

Jamie Carragher offered a lacerating analysis of United’s performance against Spurs on Saturday on Sky Sports on Monday night and suggested things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved if there is not marked improvement. Steven Gerrard questioned why United opted to invest £50m of their summer budget in Andrey Santos, an unused substitute in the last three league games, insisted the back four was not good enough and questioned the work ethic.

And it was interesting to see Carrick alongside his mate Wayne Rooney just now pitchside. Rooney told the Stick to United podcast that captain Bruno Fernandes looks “fed up” and ready to explode at any moment.

It would have been pretty unthinkable for Carrick not to run with a three-man midfield here, not just because of the wide open spaces opponents have exploited this season but when you look at the back line United are fielding. Dalot at left back, two youngsters in Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven and a horribly out of form Lisandro Maríinez.

Nor has Senne Lammens looked convincing this term. Matheus Cunha has been dropped – not before time – and I expect to see Fernandes playing off the right. There’s going to a big onus on Rashford on the left. I’m not sure if he is fully fit but he’s going to be important.

It’s fantastic. It’s where we want to be, these games, these competitions. It’s as tough a place as you can come to. They’ve got a really good history in this competition and it’s where we want to come to challenge and test ourselves. We have put ourselves in this position, got a good start at home and now this is our first away game.

We want a reaction, of course. A positive reaction [to Saturday’s poor performance]. It hasn’t gone how we wanted, how we expected so far but it’s been fine margins in some of those games. It can go both ways but the reality is where we are at now.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

#1289. The Dominik Szoboszlai dilemma: One of Europe's best midfielders who Liverpool must build around? Or a square peg who they play better without? This is what Andoni Iraola should do

Published: 21:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EDT, 3 November 2026

The folks in Liverpool’s commercial team devoted a fair portion of last season chasing after Dominik Szoboszlai.

As the club's player of the month more often than not, the Hungarian was obliged to fulfil a swathe of sponsorship duties and, like for many defenders last season, tying down Szoboszlai was not always easy. But he always completed these extracurricular activities, and was rewarded with a bumper new contract.

The midfielder was the standard-setter in pre-season and made vice-captain, with an eye on becoming the next man to wear the armband permanently when Virgil van Dijk eventually leaves. Szoboszlai’s role as protagonist continued in Andoni Iraola’s first competitive match with a last-gasp thunderous strike at Newcastle. Everything at Liverpool, it seemed, revolved around this handsome, chiseled star with a swagger.

Fast forward two months, however, and that's no longer the case. Szoboszlai has gone from first name on the teamsheet to having to fight for a starting spot. For some fans, he has become the scapegoat.

That seems wholly unfair but they point to the fact his half an hour from the bench against Arsenal coincided with Liverpool ceding control, balance and threat. Before that, Szoboszlai had missed four-and-a-half games – he went off injured early in a win at Brentford – and the Reds won all of them.

So, are Liverpool really better without the Hungarian? Let’s analyse both sides of the argument.

Would Andoni Iraola (right) really be better off without Dominik Szoboszlai (right)?

FOR: Drop him, he doesn’t fit Iraola’s system

The case against Szoboszlai revolves around balance, control and space.

Is it a coincidence that Florian Wirtz’s best run in a Liverpool shirt came in the last month, when the German had two midfielders behind him who were happy to do the defensive dirty work?

With both Szoboszlai and Wirtz in the side, it feels like the pair get in each other’s way and try to occupy the same positions, and Liverpool in turn are vulnerable to the counter-attack.

Alexis Mac Allister is enjoying his best form in well over a year and likes to arrive late into the box, but he cannot do this with Szoboszlai next to him as it leaves his team too exposed going the other way.

Young Trey Nyoni is a classy midfielder who thrives at dropping deep to start attacks and bait opposition presses. The 19-year-old is happy to sit back and allow those in front of him to thrive, such as Mac Allister playing a box-to-box role.

When Nyoni went off for Szoboszlai against Arsenal, Iraola’s side lost this balance and their chances of getting back into the game dwindled.

When Trey Nyoni went off for Szoboszlai against Arsenal, Iraola’s side lost this balance and their chances of getting back into the game dwindled

Szoboszlai is arrogant but has every right to be.

On his day, he is one of the best midfielders in Europe. A goal threat with one of the fiercest long shots in the game, with dead-ball precision, he is every bit the player Liverpool thought they were buying from RB Leipzig in 2023.

The midfielder has an engine akin to Declan Rice and is tireless in his work rate.

Surely, any team would want him and he is so talented that managers should build around him. As shown last term, he can win matches on his own. Despite his recent lay-off, he is barely injured and is a standard-bearer on the training pitch.

Iraola’s system is a 4-2-3-1 on paper but the Basque wants a bit of everything from his midfield: one No6, one No8 and one No10. Szoboszlai can play each of those roles. He has a tattoo of a Steven Gerrard quote and is the closest player to the former skipper that Anfield has seen since.

Internally, Liverpool believe Szoboszlai’s best years are ahead of him. In signing him up to a five-year deal at the end of last season – a process led by former sporting director Richard Hughes with the player’s agent Matyas Esterhazy – the Reds hierarchy were glad to stave off any future approaches from the likes of Real Madrid.

On his day, he is one of the best midfielders in Europe. Surely, any team would want him and he is so talented that managers should build around him

There are four solutions, two of which are outlined above: drop him and have a more balanced midfield or play him and benefit from his goal-scoring and creative powers, plus leadership and relentless running.

Another option may not be popular but there is a Wirtz-shaped elephant in the room. Does Iraola bench Wirtz and play Szoboszlai as the No10?

He’d have fewer defensive duties so the control and balance remains, but the Hungarian would pop up in dangerous areas to cause issues. Wirtz is a creative wizard when on form but how many times does he pass up an opportunity to shoot? Szoboszlai would already be wheeling away in celebration by the time Wirtz has made his mind up on what to do with an attack.

And then there is the compromise of Szoboszlai at right back. The player himself does not like it as he feels less important in that position, but it solves a lot of issues including all the aforementioned balance and control quirks. It also adds one thing that is bothering Iraola – creativity and attacking verve from right back.

The downside of this is Liverpool would lose the defensive acumen and physicality of aerial presence of Ronald Araujo, who is currently enjoying cult hero status at right back.

Szoboszlai is a strong right back but does not like playing there as he believes he has less influence on the game

The best teams build around the best players. There are always similar debates around Erling Haaland at Manchester City and anyone who argues the case to drop him is made to look silly.

So I will say the same about Szoboszlai. It is on Iraola to make it work. Most managers would kill for a depth of midfield talent like he has. Why not play him at right back? It solves multiple issues at once and Liverpool can finally replace the creativity Trent Alexander-Arnold used to bring from that role.

If Liverpool are seeing a game out, they can push Szoboszlai to the No 10, sub off Wirtz and bring on a true defender to help the physical battle.

Liverpool will be reunited with an old friend on Wednesday – and former cult hero Dirk Kuyt is relishing the chance to beat his old team.

Kuyt, played 285 times for the Reds between 2006 and 2012, scoring 71 times – and will face his old team for the first time on Wednesday as manager of Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

The Dutchman took over last week after a spell as assistant manager and said: ‘As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me.

‘It will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we're in, I'm not here for myself. I'm here for the club and that's what is important – to show the fans who deserve much more.

‘If we show up tomorrow with good energy, with passion and there to play, it can be a very special night.

‘Liverpool are an amazing team but so are Fenerbahce. If the fans show up, I think Europe will see how big this fan base is.’

Liverpool have happy memories in Istanbul having won this competition here in 2005 – though they lost twice to Galatasaray in Turkey last season, in the league phase and then last-16.

Fenerbahce play on the Asian side of the city and have familiar faces such as Romelu Lukaku, N'Golo Kante, Ederson, Nathan Ake and Mason Greenwood.

Liverpool will be without midfielder Ryan Gravenberch, who has a heel problem.

Boss Andoni Iraola said he liked a lot of the performance against Arsenal on Sunday but his side still need to improve.

‘It is difficult when you lose but honestly I am happy with a lot of things from the other day,’ he said. ‘I liked a lot of things but we still need to improve, especially attacking the box.'

#1288. AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?

AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

Let's start with people's real world fears about AI. Here's a sample of people we asked:

Sebastian, 22, says it'll be an AI-powered robot uprising that finally wipes out humanity: "I think that'll take some time," he says, admitting his dystopia owes a lot to the 2004 film "I, Robot."

Luisa, 19, has heard the rumors too. Her fear is what happens when these tools get into the wrong hands. "I'm more afraid of people," she says. "Powerful people."

Pilar, 25, is pessimistic about humanity's prospects. "The world is going down," she says. "Hopefully after my lifetime."

In 2026, AI systems have repeatedly slipped out of human control — and at some of the world's largest AI companies.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta have all disclosed in 2026 that their AI agents escaped the controlled test environments.

Agents are AI systems that don't just answer questions but act — running code, browsing the web, clicking through systems — on their own.

"It feels a bit crazy how powerful these models have become." Holz told DW. "I didn't anticipate they'd be so obsessed with solving tasks and that they'd start to do things we never [foresaw]."

Holz is one of 16 authors of ExploitGym. ExploitGym is an AI benchmark published in May 2026 by a team led by the University of California, Berkeley, with researchers from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. It is a standardized test of cybersecurity capabilities and vulnerabilities.

Its 898 challenges test whether AI agents can turn known software bugs into working attacks. Each one runs inside a sandbox — a sealed-off digital space, cut off from the internet, so nothing the agent does can reach anything real. That's the theory, anyway.

In July, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI models had escaped from their sandbox.

They were running an internal ExploitGym test with the models' safety refusals switched off, a setting that lets evaluators measure what a model is capable of rather than what it will decline to do.

Failing the task, the models went looking for a shortcut instead, and found a flaw in the software meant to keep them sealed in. It let them onto the open internet.

From there they worked out that Hugging Face, a site where AI developers store and share models and data, probably held the answer to the test.

So, they broke in and went looking for it, organizing the effort on message boards they set up themselves. The behavior was not instructed, according to OpenAI's account of the incident.

Hugging Face detected the intrusion and shut it down before OpenAI connected it to its own test. No customer data was reportedly taken.

"What happened is really a bit of science fiction," Holz said.

Then, Google confirmed that its Gemini model had guessed or found login credentials and accessed three real companies' websites during a May test run by the independent evaluator Irregular — an intrusion Google learned of in July 2026 and disclosed weeks later.

Anthropic's and Meta's escapes happened in sandboxes run by the same firm, which has said it notified the labs in late July 2026 and that it has since fixed the flaws.

In late September 2026, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent had broken into a statistics portal belonging to Medicare, Australia's public health system, reaching non-public files and writing data into a government server. No patient records were reportedly touched.

The incidents have revived older fears. If agents can program each other, where does that end? Could it lead to what philosopher Nick Bostrom has called a "paperclip maximizer"?

Bostrom's thought experiment imagines a machine given one simple goal: Make as many paperclips as possible.

The machine pursues the task so single-mindedly that it eventually treats humans as raw material standing in the way.

"For the intermediate future, I do not see any kind of scientific evidence that there could be this super intelligence that autonomously decides, 'Okay, let's kill,'" said Holz.

Rogue software needs vast datacenters to run, he said, which makes it visible. And the internet is built from parts that can keep working independently of one another.

But the AI escapes and hacks in 2026 were noticed late. Google learned of Gemini's intrusions two months after they happened, and OpenAI told Australia about the Medicare breach nearly three months after the event.

Holz said he expects a different kind of threat: Bad actors turning capable AI on critical infrastructure, mass compromise of ordinary machines, or chatbots used to manipulate information at scale and destabilize politics.

No, Europe cannot easily compete with China, according to experts.

France's Mistral and Germany's open-source Soofi project lag behind the frontier labs — a handful of US and Chinese firms building the most advanced models. Europe lacks the datacenter capacity to train systems at that scale, which leaves it dependent on non-European models, and largely subject to US or Chinese export controls.

For Holz, the more pressing gap is expertise. "What we definitely need to see is how we can build up more competence in the area of security, AI, and especially the intersection of both," he said.

Be skeptical of what the companies themselves claim, Holz said. They have a financial interest in the conversation, he said, particularly ahead of a stock market listing. "There's also fear mongering, or a bit of hype, about how advanced these models get."

Holz uses AI daily, as do his children. His nine-year-old generates coloring book pages. His 12-year-old uses it for homework, but has already learned the hard way that it lies and that "it's sometimes wrong."

#1287. Athletic Club academy trio score first senior goals in 6-1 Copa del Rey win at Prat

Three academy players scored their first goals for Athletic Club's senior side inside four minutes as Edin Terzić's team beat Prat 6-1 in the Copa del Rey. The late burst came from substitutes in a side rotated with the Basque derby in mind.

On Thursday 29 October, Athletic met Prat in the Copa del Rey round of 128. The tie was played at the Estadi La Feixa Llarga in L’Hospitalet de Llobregat. Its closing stages belonged to Athletic’s academy.

Each of the late scorers had come off the bench. Selton Sánchez finished the night with the sixth goal, teed up by Vizcay, whose own strike had started the flurry.

Aritz Conde earned an 8.2 rating from the data provider for his half-hour on the pitch. Imga, aged just 17, had made his first-team debut alongside Vizcay against Getafe the previous Sunday.

EFE reported that Athletic picked a starting XI shaped by the coming Basque derby, giving chances to players such as Yohaneko, Sannadi and Nico Serrano. Those changes did not slow the visitors.

Maroan Sannadi opened the scoring in the 29th minute. Robert Navarro doubled the lead two minutes later. Mikel Jauregizar provided both assists. Gustavo Reinke pulled one back for Prat in the 33rd minute, set up by Álex Plaza. Serrano restored the two-goal cushion three minutes later from a Jesús Areso pass.

The statistics show how one-sided the night was. Athletic had 68% of the ball and 20 shots from inside the box. They put 12 attempts on target, against 2 from the hosts. Prat’s goalkeeper was kept busy with six saves. Navarro earned the top rating of 9.2, with seven key passes in 86 minutes.

Miguel Ángel Motoso’s Prat came into the tie after beating San Rafael 5-1 and 5-0 in their two previous matches. The draw carried an echo for Athletic. Their run to their most recent Copa title began on 1 November 2023 against another Liga Élite Catalana side, about 22 km from L’Hospitalet.

Sergio García, the B-team coach, led the side from the touchline at the Estadio de la Cerámica. The game was the opening match of the LaLiga round.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

The giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”

But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1284. Simeone equals Luis Aragonés’s LaLiga wins record as Atlético Madrid beat Levante 2-0

Atlético Madrid won 2-0 at Levante on Saturday, making it a milestone afternoon for Diego Simeone. Barcelona are next up in the league, and one more victory would give him the coaching record on his own.

Atlético Madrid’s trip to Valencia ended with a milestone for their coach. It took the Argentine 565 LaLiga matches in charge to reach the mark, according to Club Atlético de Madrid.

The visitors went in at the interval a goal up. Álex Baena supplied the pass for their second. Earlier, Morten Hjulmand had a goal ruled out by VAR in the 17th minute. Levante coach Luís Castro was shown a yellow card for dissent a minute later.

The scoreline did not reflect the balance of chances. Levante shot 14 times from inside the box, while Atlético managed 3. The hosts’ expected goals reached 1.33, against 0.63 for the visitors.

Jan Oblak was the difference. Around the tenth minute, he made a crucial one-handed save to deny Dani Requena, Infobae (EFE) reported. The goalkeeper finished with a rating of 8.08.

Atlético had more of the ball, with 54% possession and 560 passes to Levante’s 450. Simeone made two double changes. Jonathan David and Sørloth replaced Lee Kang-In and Julián Álvarez in the 67th minute. Le Normand and Lookman came on for Barrios and Baena in the 76th.

The result was Atlético’s seventh league win in a row. It briefly took them top of the table. The teams’ last meeting, on 31 January 2026, had ended 0-0 in Valencia.

Simeone already leads Aragonés on wider measures at the club. Across all official competitions with Atlético, he has 479 wins from 813 games. Aragonés managed 308 wins from 612 games there. The club credits Simeone with eight trophies as coach, two more than Aragonés’s six.

The coming weeks carry real weight. From 11 games, Atlético have nine wins, one draw and one defeat. Real Madrid sit third on 24 points from 10 games.

Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert

Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert

The Rub’ al Khali is the world’s largest sand sea, covering almost a third of the Arabian peninsula.

The desert, whose name translates to The Empty Quarter, was once part of the lush savannah known as ‘Green Arabia’ – the periodic blooming of the region as ice age climatic shifts brought more rainfall.

Evidence of ancient humans abounds in the regions around the desert, but an expedition into the interior has returned empty handed. The surprising absence of stone tools and other signs of human occupation has led archaeologists to a new theory of the factors governing human migration, that ancient peoples needed not just water to settle, but stone as well.

#1282. Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen

Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?

On Thursday, October 8, at around 1:00 p.m. CEST, all eyes in the literary world will be set on Stockholm.

That's when the new permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, Ingrid Carlberg, will hold a press conference to announce the winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in literature, marking the end of a lengthy selection process that officially began a year earlier.

The Swedish Academy is the body responsible for awarding the prize. Its 18 members consist of writers, professors and intellectuals.

In September of the previous year, the Academy's Nobel Committee sends forms to hundreds of individuals and organizations eligible to submit nominations for the Nobel Prize in literature.

According to the Nobel Prize website, these include professors of literature and linguistics at universities and colleges, previous Nobel laureates in literature and the heads of writers' associations that represent the literary community in their respective countries. Anyone from one of these groups who has not received a form may also submit a nomination.

"The list can reach 200 names per year of nominated authors," explains Gisele Sapiro, research director at France's National Centre for Scientific Research. She studies how the Nobel Prize, as a global institution, influences the international circulation of literature, power dynamics in the literary world and translation markets.

"The committee can also add names itself, such as authors who were nominated in previous years," she says.

In the spring, the Nobel Committee then selects five names through a multistage process and presents them to the Academy. Over the summer, Academy members read the nominees' works and discuss them. The Academy always announces the decision in early October.

As for the criteria the Academy uses to make its decision, it prefers to keep them to itself.

The public doesn't learn which nominees missed out until 50 years later — that's how long the Academy waits before releasing the list.

Sometimes decades pass between an author's first nomination and actually receiving the prize. Danish writer Johannes V. Jensen, who won the Nobel Prize in literature in 1944, waited 40 years. Doris Lessing received the award in 2007 after 35 years, while Thomas Mann, who won in 1929, had to wait 27 years.

In his will, Alfred Nobel, the prize's founder, stipulated that it should be awarded to the person who had produced "the most outstanding work in an idealistic direction." That leaves plenty of room for interpretation.

According to Gisele Sapiro, the Academy aims to honor ambitious, influential literature that has, for example, given rise to a new literary movement. "At the same time, the work has to be universal, being able to transcend its own culture," she says.

Translations can be one indication of this. "I noted in my research, however, that all the laureates since 1990 had been translated into English, French and German — except for Abdulrazak Gurnah [the Tanzanian-British 2021 Nobel laureate], who had not been translated into German before winning — meaning that I think these three languages are the most important," Sapiro explains.

Sapiro says it is also a major advantage if nominees have already won other major literary awards, such as the International Man Booker Prize, the Cervantes Prize or the Büchner Prize.

Politics can also influence the Swedish Academy's decisions.

On several occasions, the prize has gone to writers who openly opposed the regimes in their home countries, such as Belarusian writer Svetlana Alexievich in 2015. She is an outspoken critic of authoritarian President Alexander Lukashenko.

Genre, on the other hand, does not matter. In the past, laureates have been honored not only for novels but also for poetry and plays. In 2016, singer-songwriter Bob Dylan received the prize for his song lyrics.

So far, only 33 of the 122 laureates have come from outside Europe. There is also a clear gender imbalance: only in the past eight years have men and women alternated as winners, significantly increasing women's share of the total number of laureates to 14.9%.

This article was originally written in German.

#1281. Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty

Athletic Club beat Real Sociedad 2-1 at San Mamés on Sunday 1 November to end their rivals' run of four straight league wins. The visitors have formally disputed the first-half penalty that decided the derby, while Athletic lost another striker to injury.

Every goal in the Bilbao derby arrived before half-time.

Nico Williams provided the assist for the opening goal. Luka Sučić equalised on the half-hour. A crowd of 50,092 watched the game.

Before kick-off, Unai Simón presented his Yashin Trophy to the home crowd. A minute’s silence was also held for the victims of the Urda rail accident.

The visitors left Bilbao angry about the decisive spot-kick. In its official match report, Real Sociedad called it a penalty that never was and criticised VAR for not stepping in. The club statement added that the chip inside the match ball shows Jon Aramburu made contact with the ball in his challenge on Nico Williams.

Pellegrino Matarazzo said that for him it was clearly not a penalty. The Real Sociedad coach could not understand why VAR had not intervened to cancel it. He was booked for dissent in the 65th minute, a minute after Mamadou Sarr received a yellow card for the same offence. Referee Alejandro Hernandez showed Real Sociedad four yellow cards in total, against two for Athletic.

The statistics point in two directions. Real Sociedad dominated the ball, completing 514 accurate passes to Athletic’s 307. Terzić’s side created the clearer chances, however. Unai Simón made four saves, while Álex Remiro made one. Sučić was the highest-rated player on the pitch at 7.52.

The victory came at a cost. Maroan Sannadi felt his hamstring early in the game. Athletic will need one or two more days to know how long he will be out. His injury follows Gorka Guruzeta’s serious knee injury at Valencia on 17 October, which left the squad short of strikers.

With 83 minutes on the pitch, Navarro created four key passes and was rated 7.2.

The win was Athletic’s third in a row across all competitions, after a 6-1 victory over Prat and a 4-0 win against Getafe. They sit seventh, two points behind Sevilla. Real Betis are four points clear of Real Sociedad.

#1280. Barcelona rout Alavés 6-1 to retake LaLiga lead before top-two clash with Atlético

Barcelona beat Alavés 6-1 at Spotify Camp Nou to go back to the top of LaLiga. The win came with a reshuffled defence and sets up a meeting of the top two at the Metropolitano.

Atlético Madrid had gone top of LaLiga earlier on 31 October by winning at Levante. Within hours, Barcelona took the place back. Hansi Flick’s side dismantled Alavés in front of their own fans. The result ended a two-game losing run after defeats to PSG and Real Madrid.

Barcelona have scored 46 goals and conceded 12, a goal difference of +34, according to the official LaLiga table. Atlético have scored 22 and conceded 8.

This was Barcelona’s first test since the Clásico. Real Madrid won that game 2-1 at Camp Nou on 25 October. Kylian Mbappé scored twice, the second in the 87th minute, after Raphinha had equalised on 61 minutes. That defeat ended a run of nine straight league wins at the start of the season.

Raphinha opened the scoring in the 8th minute. Fermín López added a second in the 23rd. Raphinha struck again in the 41st, and Lamine Yamal made it four in first-half stoppage time. Barcelona held 77% of the ball, in front of a crowd of 53,523.

Yamal’s second goal, in the 64th minute, was first ruled out for offside. A VAR review showed his run was onside. He was taken off to a standing ovation soon afterwards, with Gordon replacing him.

The former Newcastle winger scored in the 81st minute, his first league goal for the club. He ran on to a through ball from Rodri and chipped the goalkeeper. Mariano Díaz pulled one back for Alavés in the 84th minute.

Absences left Flick short at the back. Fariñas started at right-back and played the full 90 minutes. Frenkie de Jong moved to centre-back alongside Cubarsí. João Cancelo completed the back four at left-back. Gerard Martín replaced De Jong in the 82nd minute.
